methodology: Verse-specific preliminary comparison of Qur'an 12:46–50 with Genesis 41. English ESV Genesis 41:14–36 read; Hebrew MT, LXX, Syriac Peshitta, manuscript witnesses, critical apparatus, compositional dating and direct transmission NOT checked. Never publish as verified on this basis.
previous_checkpoint: Draft PR #430, Yusuf 12:41–45; no merge claimed

assessments.evidence: The freed prisoner asks Joseph to explain seven fat and seven lean cows and grain ears; compare Genesis 41:17–24, where Pharaoh recounts the dream directly to Joseph.

Joseph prescribes seven years of cultivation and retaining harvest in its ears except for consumption; Genesis 41:29,34–36 likewise has seven plentiful years and storage, but specifies a fifth collected by Pharaoh's officials.
Seven hard years consume reserves with a little preserved; Genesis 41:30–31,36 predicts seven famine years and stored food, without the same expression about consuming prior stores.
An ensuing year of relief and pressing produce is specified; Genesis 41:29–36 speaks of seven plenty then seven famine years, not an explicitly numbered subsequent year of rain/pressing.
The king sends for Joseph, but Joseph requests an investigation into women who cut their hands; Genesis 41:14 has Pharaoh summon Joseph directly, with no analogous demand for investigation.

dossier.title: Joseph's interpretation, grain reserves and release: Qur'an 12:46–50 / Genesis 41
dossier.overview: Both narratives connect the ruler's dream of seven cows and grain with a seven-year agricultural cycle and famine preparations. Qur'an puts the interpretation in a message carried by the freed prisoner and has Joseph request vindication before release; Genesis brings Joseph directly to Pharaoh and adds a fifth-part administrative levy.
dossier.chronology_and_witnesses: Genesis traditions predate Islam, but the date of composition of the narrative is debated and must not be equated with dates of extant manuscripts. Compare MT, LXX and Peshitta before publishing. Qur'anic text is seventh-century CE; its precise relationship to any individual witness is not established.
dossier.scholarly_caveat: Shared narrative does not establish copying or the direction/medium of transmission. The distinctive 'pressing' in Qur'an 12:49 and the women's inquiry in 12:50 require separate comparative research.
